title: Beef Bourguignon
subtitle: Slow-braised beef with pancetta, mushrooms, and red wine
excerpt: Beef bourguignon is a long, slow braise from Burgundy. Beef chuck is browned with pancetta and vegetables, then cooked low and slow in red wine and stock until deeply tender. It is even better the next day.
sourceNotes: Boeuf bourguignon is a classic French braise from the Burgundy region, traditionally made with Pinot Noir. It was popularised in English-speaking countries through Julia Child's 1961 cookbook.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freezes very well for up to 3 months. Defrost in the fridge overnight and reheat gently.
recipe.batchNotes: Double the batch and freeze half. Use a large enough pot.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make up to 2 days ahead and refrigerate. The flavour improves with time.
recipe.temperatureNote: This is a hob braise throughout. No oven needed.

content.text: The key step is browning the beef properly before it braises. Pat the meat dry and cook it in batches. Do not crowd the pot or it will steam instead of colour. Good browning gives the sauce its depth.

items.prepNote: or use a robust red wine

content.text: Pat the beef dry with kitchen paper. Season well with salt and pepper.
Melt the butter in the stockpot over a high heat. Brown the beef in batches for 2 to 3 minutes per side. Remove and set aside.
Add the pancetta to the same pot. Cook for 3 minutes until lightly golden. Remove and set aside.
Reduce the heat to medium. Add the onion and carrot. Cook for 5 minutes.
Add the garlic, tomato puree, and flour. Stir and cook for 1 minute.
Pour in the wine and stock. Stir and scrape up any browned bits from the bottom.
Return the beef and pancetta to the pot. Add the thyme and bay leaves. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Cover and cook on the lowest heat for 2 hours, stirring occasionally.
Add the mushrooms. Cook uncovered for a further 20 minutes until the sauce has thickened.
Taste and adjust seasoning. Remove bay leaves and thyme stalks. Scatter over parsley and serve.

items.symptom: The beef is still tough after 2 hours.
items.cause: The braise was at too low a heat or the cuts were too large.
items.fix: Keep cooking on a slightly higher simmer for another 30 minutes.

items.symptom: The sauce is too thin at the end.
items.cause: The lid was on throughout, stopping reduction.
items.fix: Simmer uncovered on medium heat for 10 to 15 minutes.

items.symptom: The sauce tastes acidic and sharp.
items.cause: Vinegar or wine was not cooked out long enough.
items.fix: Continue simmering and add a small pinch of sugar to balance.
